source.title: Dynamical Batching: How Class-Cycling Training Shapes the Internal Structure of Neural Networks
source.authors: N. Ratier-Werbin; Samuel Lozano; Miguel Ruíz-García

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether training reaches high training accuracy under different batching protocols, including CIFAR-10 CNNs, but its intervention is cyclic batch composition rather than the training conditions emphasized by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports training-accuracy outcomes for its own runs. Related-work results cited in the paper are not included as rows. Grid-wide accuracy maps and described failure regions are not separately rowed where the text does not give assignable numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study measures training classification accuracy in CIFAR-10 CNNs trained with SGD under uniform and cyclic class batching, bearing on V1 in a new training setting. Its synthetic MLP experiments do not match V1's CNN and dataset scope. It does not test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the paper's central structural result: cyclic class emphasis produces a smaller, more persistent set of switching weights in synthetic MLPs, including where accuracy does not improve. It rescues the small spiral MLP and modestly improves test accuracy in two narrow CIFAR-10 CNNs while reducing training fit. The authors stress architecture and hyperparameter dependence and do not establish that weight localization causes the accuracy gains.
record.recipe_differences: Changes class composition of mini-batches over time while keeping the loss and optimizer unchanged; CIFAR-10 CNNs use SGD and the toy MLP uses Adam. Does not test the listed original recipes as a controlled comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on batching amplitude and period; large amplitudes with short periods can collapse training. Across CIFAR-10 architectures, test-accuracy gains beyond seed noise occur only in the two narrowest models.

fits_no_version.finding: On the spiral, the small MLP plateaus under uniform batching even with twice the training budget, while cyclic batching fits the data; the wider MLP fits under both protocols.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these synthetic classification tasks, attainable training fit depends jointly on MLP width and the temporal distribution of class sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Cyclic batching concentrates class-switching changes in a smaller, more persistent set of weights, including settings without an accuracy gain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal class emphasis can change the localization and persistence of parameter motion independently of improvements in training fit.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 accuracy effect is selected from a grid using test accuracy, which the authors say biases the maximum upward. Each configuration uses 5 seeds. Training accuracy is evaluated on 5,000-example subsets. The authors do not isolate whether width, baseline test accuracy, or another model property explains which CNNs benefit.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the many grid cells or figure-only failure regions; the text reports aggregate descriptions but not individually assignable training-accuracy values for those cells. CIFAR rows focus on UB baselines and best-test configurations reported in Table V.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam training of CNNs, early stopping, and classification error on the complete CIFAR-10 training set. The architecture sweep does not isolate model size as the cause of incomplete fitting.
Teacher-student realizability, verified spurious local minima, their frequency under gradient descent, and adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with increasing depth and matched comparisons with identity shortcuts.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, training speed attributable to initialization, and maximum trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature evolution, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Matched normalization ablations, training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No original-source exclusion applies. CIFAR-10 results support conclusions about evaluated training subsets. Test-based configuration selection limits interpretation of the selected DB recipes as tests of maximum attainable training fit. Grid-wide collapse regions and aggregate grid results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD versus Adam as a comparison, or smaller models and early stopping as general conditions. CIFAR-10 CNN results use cyclic batch composition and report selected configurations alongside uniform-batching baselines.
